samples.summary: The new `drag` destination is a fourth reader-citation door that the per-run surface pin (`checkSurfaceScope`) does not inspect — `action.to.reader` bypasses the only exact-name enforcement of the run's assigned surface
samples.evidence: `checkSurfaceScope` builds its `cited` list from exactly three places: `action.reader` (read/wait), `action.target.reader`, and `action.expect.read` (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187). Its own docstring (lines 176-179) says the target's `reader` is the door "easy to miss" and the test file enumerates the same three (hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs:169-179, "Removing any one of them from the check reopens it"). This change adds a FOURTH reader-bearing field, `action.to` (hunt-ui-probe.mjs:163 `assertTarget(action.to, ...)`, runner drag case at hunt-ui-runner.mjs:298), and neither the check nor its test is extended. Vector: a run pinned to `slides` (or `doc`) emits `{type:"drag", target:{role:"button",name:"x"}, to:{reader:"sheet.cellCenter", args:["A1"]}}`. Step 2 `assertSafeActionPlan` passes it, because that validator deliberately only bounds reader NAMESPACES (`sheet.` is a legal prefix, hunt-ui-probe.mjs:79-81). Step 3 `checkSurfaceScope` returns null, because `to` is not in `cited`. The runner then calls `readValue(page, "sheet.cellCenter", ...)` unguarded (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:214 via `resolveTarget`), i.e. an out-of-scope reader is invoked on the caller's behalf and its refusal (or, for any reader that does not need the unmounted handle, its VALUE — see the separate error-message leak finding) comes back on the model's channel. Today the blast radius is limited because page.tsx mounts exactly one surface handle (`controller.setDoc`/`setSheet`/`setSlides` at page.tsx:402/477/465 are mutually exclusive), so `requireSheet` refuses at runtime — the pin is bypassed but the data is not reachable. That is a second, unrelated control doing the pin's job: the gate itself is now incomplete, reads as complete ("anything from a surface this run was not assigned" is listed as a hard guarantee in the module header, lines 27-33), and the same hole covers `to.reader` naming an UNKNOWN reader, which `checkSurfaceScope` is also the only component that rejects by exact name.

samples.summary: A reader's full value is echoed into the drag/click failure message, so a non-`read` action can return page state to the caller — the new `to` field doubles this channel and combines with the surface-pin gap above
samples.evidence: `resolveTarget` throws ``target reader ${target.reader} did not return finite {x,y}, got ${JSON.stringify(point)}`` (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:219). The message is stored on the observation and rendered straight back to the model as `FAILED: drag — <error>` (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:269, unclipped; only `redactSecrets` is applied). So `{type:"drag", target:{...}, to:{reader:"dom.snapshot"}}` — or any reader whose value is not `{x,y}` — returns that reader's serialized value through an action the design states returns only whether it landed (module header, hunt-ui-tool.mjs:15-19). Pre-existing via `click.target` rather than introduced here, but this change adds a second such field and, per the finding above, `to` is the one field the surface pin does not filter, so the leaked reader need not be in scope for the run. Impact is bounded: `dom.*` readers are already in scope for every run, and ground-C grounding still fails closed because `lastSnapshot` is only populated for an explicit `read` of `dom.snapshot` (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:430-432). Hardening: report the reader name and the value's shape, not `JSON.stringify(point)`.
searchedFor: read hunt-ui-runner.mjs resolveTarget (209-224) and observeAction error capture (381-433)
read hunt-ui-tool.mjs renderUiObservation (265-323) to confirm the error string is returned to the model without clipping
grep `lastSnapshot` in hunt-ui-tool.mjs to check whether a leaked snapshot could be used as ground C

samples.summary: `slides.pointAt`'s off-slide bound fails OPEN on a non-finite computed point — unlike `slides.elementCenter`, it has no `Number.isFinite` guard before `isOffSlide`
samples.evidence: `isOffSlide` is four `<`/`>` comparisons (slides-seed.ts:70-71), and every comparison against NaN is false, so a NaN point is reported as ON the slide. `slides.elementCenter` guards against exactly this before calling it (bridge.ts:631-633, `refuse(... non-finite point ...)`), and the new `slides.pointAt` does not: at bridge.ts:556-558 `scale = origin.width / handle.slideWidth` is Infinity if `slideWidth` is 0 (and NaN if it is undefined/NaN), and `Math.round(origin.left + 0 * Infinity)` is NaN, which then passes the bounds check and is returned as a usable point. The caller-supplied `x`/`y` themselves are constrained by the new `asNumber` (bridge.ts:192-201), so the trigger is a degenerate handle rather than caller input, and the runner's own `Number.isFinite` check on the resolved point (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:218) stops a NaN reaching `page.mouse`. So this is hardening, not an exploit — but the boundary guard that this reader's docstring presents as the reason it is not a 'screen-pixel escape hatch' is the one that fails open, and it is the only bound on where `pointAt` can aim.
searchedFor: compared the guard order in slides.elementCenter (bridge.ts:627-645) with slides.pointAt (bridge.ts:549-566) and slides.handleCenter (582-608)
checked asNumber/asString (bridge.ts:192-209) for what caller input can reach the arithmetic

verdict.reason: The absence itself is real: checkSurfaceScope (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187) cites only action.reader, action.target.reader and action.expect.read, its sole call site is line 405, and I found no other agent-side component that name-checks action.to.reader against the run's surface. I could not produce a counterexample for the missing check. But the security vector it claims is already guarded end-to-end, in-process, at the asset: every non-dom reader in the bridge registry (bridge.ts:294-703) dereferences its surface through requireDoc/requireSheet/requireSlides (bridge.ts:171-190), which refuses when the handle is null — including all four point-resolving readers a drag `to` could name (sheet.cellCenter:651, slides.elementCenter:612, slides.pointAt:552, slides.handleCenter:584); no reader returns a value without its handle, so the claimed value-leak branch is empty. Unknown reader names are rejected by exact name, not by prefix, at bridge.ts:728-729 (hasOwnProperty membership test) — the second property the finding attributes exclusively to checkSurfaceScope. And the mounted surface is provably the assigned surface: page.tsx:397/404/468 is one mutually-exclusive if/else setting a single handle, and the only way to remount is `goto`, which checkSurfaceScope does cover (line 198) and the tool schema makes unrepresentable (line 559). The residual observable is a refusal string ("sheet reader used while surface is doc") over a harness whose stores are seeded MemStore/MemDocStore fixtures in a local headless browser with **/auth/** stubbed (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:366) — no credential, no user data, no cross-tenant asset. Under the Security lane this is defence-in-depth completeness rather than a reachable authorization bypass; the gate-incompleteness is the correctness lens's issue, where it is already filed (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:5).
